task.name: A review finding that repeats a claim already injected into the same run is indistinguishable from a novel one, so the knowledge loop cannot be observed missing its target
task.story_text:
A review finding that repeats a claim already injected into the same run is indistinguishable from a novel one, so the knowledge loop cannot be observed missing its target

## Context

Deciding whether the prior-run knowledge loop creates net value requires a randomized comparison
accumulating over months. Separately from that verdict, there is a mechanism observation available
from a single run and not currently made.

When prior-run context is injected, the selector renders specific claims into a phase's prompt. When
the run is reviewed, the reviewer records findings. Nobody compares the two, so the case where the
loop delivered material on a subject the review then raised anyway leaves no trace.

Establishing that correspondence requires knowing which claims the author of a finding could
actually have acted on, and the current records do not support that question. Injection reaches the
planning, development and review phases alike — review manifests on the local substrate carry
non-empty inclusions — so a claim rendered into a reviewer's own prompt can prompt that reviewer to
raise it, which would register as the development agent having missed something it was never shown.
Runs also cycle: a claim injected into a later development iteration cannot explain a finding
recorded before it.

This is a missed-uptake indicator, not evidence of value. A correspondence does not establish that
usable guidance was ignored: the claim may have been irrelevant to the story, ambiguous,
contradicted by newer evidence, or actionable only in part. What it establishes is a population
worth inspecting when asking whether selection, rendering or placement is working. No verdict about
whether knowledge pays for itself derives from it.

Its value is that it yields observations at the scale of one run while a randomized comparison
accumulates, and that it compares two recorded artifacts against each other rather than resting on
any model's account of its own reasoning.

## Acceptance criteria

- A record of an injected claim identifies which phase received it, which agent role it was rendered
  to, which iteration of that phase, and when it was rendered, so that what a given author could
  have acted on is determinable from the record alone.
- The comparison considers a claim against a finding only where the claim reached the author of the
  work the finding is about, before that finding was recorded. A claim rendered only to the reviewer
  is never eligible to explain that reviewer's own finding, and a claim rendered after a finding is
  never eligible to explain it.
- Where a run received eligible injected claims and its review recorded findings, the run's record
  distinguishes findings corresponding to an eligible claim from findings not matched to one, and
  preserves which claim each correspondence refers to.
- The unmatched category is reported as not matched to an eligible injected claim. Nothing in the
  report describes an unmatched finding as novel, since failing to match establishes only the
  absence of a correspondence.
- The report presents the correspondence as an indicator of missed uptake and never as evidence that
  knowledge helped or failed to help.
- A run that received no eligible claims, or whose review recorded no findings, emits no
  correspondence and is reported as having none — distinct from a run that was compared and matched
  nothing.
- The record names the method that decided each correspondence and the version of that method, so a
  reported figure remains interpretable when the method changes.
- The method's agreement with human labelling is measured against a stored set of labelled examples
  covering correspondences, non-correspondences, and cases eligibility excludes, and that agreement
  is reported with the figures the method produces. A method whose agreement has not been measured
  reports its figures as unvalidated rather than omitting them.
- Where the comparison cannot determine whether a finding corresponds to an eligible claim, the run
  records that indeterminacy rather than classifying the finding either way, and the count of
  indeterminate findings appears beside the totals.
- Findings recorded on runs that predate claim-exposure capture are reported as uncomparable rather
  than as findings that corresponded to nothing.

## Example

A run receives a prior-run summary at the development phase whose rendered claims include one about
a coordinator-owned gate result not being derivable from an agent's report. The same run's reviewer
is separately shown a summary containing a claim about branch staleness. The review records four
findings: one restating the gate point, one restating the staleness point, two others.

The run's record then shows:

```
Prior-run uptake
  claims rendered            9   (7 to dev iter 1-2, 2 to review iter 1)
  claims eligible            7   (review-only claims excluded: not available to the author)
  review findings            4
    corresponding to an eligible claim   1  -> claim 3, run 27bb13e86070, dev iteration 1
    not matched to an eligible claim     3
    indeterminate                        0
  method: rendered-claim-overlap v2 — agreement with labelled set 0.89 (n=140)

  missed-uptake indicator only; contributes to no effectiveness verdict
```

The staleness finding is not counted as missed uptake: that claim reached only the reviewer, so the
reviewer raising it is the claim working, not the development agent ignoring it.

A run with no eligible claims shows `claims eligible 0` and no correspondence block, rather than a
block reporting zero correspondences.

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. plan_finding_registry.description: Step 1 targets the wrong boundary for complete exposure provenance. prior_run_manifest.build_manifest() is called by ContextAssembler.assemble(), whose signature only receives phase, story text, and files. Recipient role and iteration exist only at callers such as coordinator/plan_flow.py, coordinator/dev_phase.py, coordinator/review_pool.py, and coordinator/review_phase.py. Review context is assembled before per-profile prompts and may be shared across configurable review roles, so selector/manifest changes alone cannot record which role actually received each claim.

Step 2 changes the audit record shape without accounting for the repository's mandatory schema workflow. coordinator/audit.py imports its schema version from coordinator/audit_storage.py through audit_substrate.py, and tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py guarantees that added fields fail unless CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped, a MIGRATION_HELPERS entry is added, and the schema snapshot is regenerated. Read-time legacy handling also belongs in audit_storage.py, not audit.py.

The plan never persists correspondence outcomes in the run record. Step 2 stores only claim exposures, while Step 5 invokes the matcher from knowledge-effectiveness report assembly. Consequently finding classifications, claim references, indeterminacy, and the deciding method/version exist only in a recomputed report, contrary to the acceptance criteria requiring the run's record to preserve them.

Step 4 stores the human-labelled corpus in tests/fixtures while runtime code in src/theforge/knowledge_uptake_correspondence.py is expected to load and evaluate it. pyproject.toml packages src/theforge only, so installed forge knowledge-report executions cannot access tests/fixtures and would always report unvalidated or fail to load the corpus.

Step 1 claims per-claim exposure records carrying agent role, phase iteration and rendered_at can be produced by modifying only src/theforge/task/prior_run_manifest.py and prior_run_selector.py. None of that data exists on that surface. prior_run_manifest.build_manifest(selection, *, included_run_ids, phase) (prior_run_manifest.py:33) receives no claim text, no role, no iteration and no timestamp; its sole production caller is ContextAssembler.assemble() at src/theforge/task/context_assembler.py:277, and assemble() itself only takes phase, story_text, file_list (context_assembler.py:129-135) — the assembler has no concept of agent role or phase iteration. The values AC-1 demands are only known at the six call sites: dev_phase.py:1281 and :1344, review_phase.py:2559, review_pool.py:758, plan_flow.py:926, preflight_flow.py:428. Also, _evidenced_claims / _dev_grounded_claims (prior_run_selector.py:621,638) return bare claim strings that never reach the manifest, so there is no data flow from claim rendering to manifest as the plan assumes. As written, Step 1 either produces exposure records missing role/iteration (AC-1 unmet, which then makes Step 3's reviewer-only and post-finding eligibility gates unenforceable, breaking AC-2) or silently changes a signature whose caller the plan never lists.

Step 5 says it will 'replac[e] reliance on aggregate reviewer self-report for this missed-uptake observation' in knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py. _review_recurrence (knowledge_effectiveness_signals.py:260) populates RunSignals.restated_findings, which is consumed by the cohort effectiveness comparison at knowledge_effectiveness.py:166. Rewiring that field to the new correspondence matcher would both change an existing effectiveness metric's meaning and route the correspondence signal into an effectiveness verdict, which the spec forbids.

Step 3 says the matcher 'accepts persisted claim exposures and review findings' without naming the finding record, and Step 1's stated risk assumes per-finding role/timestamp data may be absent. The audit already persists finding_registry entries with finding_id, description, severity, reporter, cycle_first_seen, cycle_last_seen (coordinator/audit.py:1294-1307) — per-finding identity, reporter and cycle ordering are available, so the risk is largely retired and the fallback-to-indeterminate path should be the exception, not the assumption.

To ensure timing-based eligibility filtering is robust when precise sub-second per-finding timestamps are absent, fallback to comparing the dev_iteration at rendering against cycle_first_seen at recording to deterministically separate pre-finding and post-finding claims.

For the deterministic matching method (e.g. rendered-claim-overlap/v1), define explicit, verifiable similarity thresholds (e.g. >= 0.4 for correspondence, and [0.2, 0.4) for indeterminate) to ensure consistent agreement scores against the labelled fixture.

plan_structured.approach: Record rendered claims and their recipients inside the existing prior_run_context manifest block, stamp each review cycle with a wall-clock recorded_at so findings have a valid ordering coordinate, and derive the claim-to-finding correspondence as a pure, versioned function of the persisted record applied at the single audit-write chokepoint — which sits after carry_prior_generation_work and covers the in-flight flush too. Report the result as an eligibility-gated missed-uptake indicator, validated against a hand-labelled corpus and kept out of every effectiveness verdict.

steps.description: Record rendered claims and recipients inside the prior_run_context manifest
steps.details: Deliberately no new top-level audit section: the exposure evidence goes inside the block that already exists so it is carried, migrated and read through one path. In prior_run_selector, have _render_summary/_phase_lines return the claim strings they rendered alongside the prose (the strings _evidenced_claims and _dev_grounded_claims already produce, after the _MAX_RENDERED_CLAIMS cap, so the record holds what was actually shown), and expose them per candidate on PriorRunSelection. In prior_run_manifest.build_manifest, emit each included candidate's rendered claims as `claims: [{claim_index, claim, source_run_id}]`, and add three manifest-level fields describing the single rendering event: `agent_roles` (list — one context pack can feed several reviewer profiles, so recipients are recorded as a set rather than a scalar), `phase_iteration`, and `rendered_at` (ISO-8601 UTC, stamped at render time, never reconstructed). Thread agent_roles/phase_iteration/rendered_at through ContextAssembler.assemble() as keyword-only arguments defaulting to absent, so every existing call site and disabled_manifest() keep working unchanged.

steps.description: Pass recipient role and iteration from the coordinator phases that assemble context
steps.details: At the five sites that append to state.context_manifests (dev_phase.py:1286 and :1349, review_phase.py:2564, review_pool.py:763, plan_flow.py:932, preflight_flow.py:432), pass the recipient role(s) and the phase iteration into assemble(). Dev and plan pass the authoring role; review passes every reviewer profile the assembled pack is handed to, so a claim shown only to reviewers is identifiable as such from the record. Preflight passes its role for completeness; it is signal-only and never author-side, matching classify_cohort's existing exclusion of preflight manifests.

steps.description: Stamp each review cycle with a wall-clock recorded_at
steps.details: Findings are taken from reviews[*].findings, not finding_registry — build_reviews (audit_render.py:276-348) already emits severity/file/line/description/reviewers/reporter per cycle, which is everything eligibility and matching need, and `reviews` is a PRIOR_GENERATION_WORK_KEYS member so it is carried in lockstep with context_manifests. What is missing is only an ordering coordinate. Add `recorded_at: str | None = None` to ReviewCycleMetadata (state.py:604-644), populated with an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp where the metadata is appended (review_phase.py:1474 and :2597), and surface it on each entry in build_reviews. Default None so states deserialized from older runs load unchanged and render as an unknown time. No iteration or cycle integer is ever used to order an exposure against a finding: dev_iteration aliases RetryBudget.cycle_count which resets per review cycle, cycle numbering can be reset by human extension, and the two sequences are not comparable — wall clock is the only valid coordinate.

steps.description: Create the pure correspondence deriver
steps.details: A single pure function over a persisted audit record dict — no coordinator state, no live objects — so any reader re-derives byte-identical classifications and no writer can disagree with a reader. Reads context_manifests[*].prior_run_context (claims, agent_roles, phase_iteration, rendered_at) and reviews[*] (recorded_at, findings). Eligibility: a claim is eligible for a finding only when it was rendered to an author-side phase (plan or dev — the agents who wrote the work a review finding is about), and when its rendered_at strictly precedes the recording time of the cycle that raised the finding. A claim whose only recipients are the finding's reporter role, or reviewer roles generally, is never eligible. Classify each finding as corresponding (carrying the matched claim's source run id, claim index, phase and iteration), not_matched_to_eligible_claim, or indeterminate. Indeterminate — never matched, never unmatched — when rendered_at or recorded_at is absent, or when agent_roles or reporter is missing so eligibility cannot be decided. Distinguish, as separate whole-run states, no_eligible_claims and no_findings (each emitting no correspondence block at all) from uncomparable_pre_exposure_capture, which is what a record whose prior_run_context blocks predate claim capture reports. Similarity is deterministic token overlap with a threshold calibrated against the step-5 corpus, not chosen a priori. Export METHOD_NAME='rendered-claim-overlap' and METHOD_VERSION='v1' and stamp both into every result.

steps.description: Hand-label an example corpus from real run artifacts, before any threshold is written
steps.details: Authored before step 4's threshold exists, so the reported agreement is not the method grading its own output. Examples are drawn from real persisted artifacts — claim exposures produced by steps 1-2 and real reviews[*].findings from existing audit records — and labelled by hand. Cover true correspondences, non-correspondences, reviewer-only exclusions, post-finding exclusions, and indeterminate cases. Each example records provenance: source run id, the manifest and cycle it came from, the labeller, and the labelling date, so a reader can tell a hand-labelled example from a generated one. Include at least one example the intended method is expected to get wrong, so measured agreement is demonstrably below 1.0 rather than tautological. Stored as packaged runtime data under src/theforge/data/; [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ['src/theforge'] (pyproject.toml:34-35) already ships non-Python data from that tree, as it does for config/data/models.yaml, so pyproject.toml is not edited.

steps.description: Measure the method's agreement with the labelled corpus
steps.details: Load the packaged corpus via importlib.resources (must work from an installed wheel, not a tests/fixtures path) and run the active method/version over it, returning agreement and n. When no measurement covers the active method version, the result carries an explicit unvalidated flag and the figures are still produced — never suppressed.

steps.description: Annotate the record with the derived block at the single write chokepoint
steps.details: This is the step that answers the recurring finding. _dump_audit_atomically (audit.py:1785) is the one function both writers pass through: _write_story_audit calls carry_prior_generation_work first (line 1688) and write_live_story_audit flushes an in-flight record (line 1828). Deriving there is therefore provably after the carry, so a synthetic drop record that inherited a prior generation's context_manifests and reviews is annotated from the carried evidence, not from the pre-carry empty state. Because the deriver is pure over the record and both evidence sections are carried keys, a carried generation cannot produce a block that disagrees with its own manifests and reviews. A carried generation whose manifests predate claim capture yields uncomparable_pre_exposure_capture from the same code path — it does not need to reach a migration to be reported correctly. Annotation is idempotent (recomputed on each flush) and best-effort: a failure must not break the audit write.

steps.description: Bump the record schema and regenerate the versioned snapshot
steps.details: Bump CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION 43 -> 44 (audit_storage.py:155), add the required MIGRATION_HELPERS[43] entry keeping max(MIGRATION_HELPERS) == CURRENT - 1 (the invariant documented at audit_storage.py:2233), and regenerate tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v44.json via the REGENERATE_AUDIT_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT procedure the guard prints (test_audit_schema_guard.py:359-362, 395-407); _snapshot_path() at line 343 resolves the versioned name, and there is no generic audit_record_schema.json to create. The migration is a read-time widening: pre-v44 records keep prior_run_context blocks with no claims/rendered_at and reviews with no recorded_at, and readers must interpret their absent uptake block as uncomparable, never as compared-with-zero-matches.

steps.description: Surface the figures in knowledge signals without touching effectiveness verdicts
steps.details: Read the annotated block from the record and add it as a new, separately named field on the signals payload, re-deriving from the record when the block is absent (an older or externally-written record) so the figure is available without a rewrite. Leave _review_recurrence and RunSignals.restated_findings untouched, and do not let correspondence enter classify_cohort or any cohort comparison in knowledge_effectiveness.py — it is a within-run indicator, not a treatment effect.

steps.description: Render the uptake section in language that claims only what it establishes
steps.details: A Prior-run uptake section reporting: claims rendered (with a per-phase/role breakdown), claims eligible (naming reviewer-only exclusions as not available to the author), review findings, findings corresponding to an eligible claim with the claim each refers to, findings not matched to an eligible claim, and indeterminate count beside the totals. Method name and version on every figure, with agreement and n or an explicit unvalidated marker. A run with no eligible claims or no findings prints the zero and no correspondence block, visibly distinct from a compared run that matched nothing; a pre-capture run prints uncomparable. The word 'novel' never appears for an unmatched finding, and the section carries an explicit line that this is a missed-uptake indicator contributing to no effectiveness verdict.

Where the comparison cannot determine whether a finding corresponds to an eligible claim, the run records that indeterminacy rather than classifying the finding either way, and the count of indeterminate findings appears beside the totals.
Findings recorded on runs that predate claim-exposure capture are reported as uncomparable rather than as findings that corresponded to nothing.

risks.description: Exposures and findings could be ordered against each other using non-comparable counters. dev_iteration aliases RetryBudget.cycle_count (reset each review cycle) while cycle_first_seen is a review-cycle number, and human extension can reset review_cycle — so a later dev exposure can carry a smaller number than an earlier finding.
risks.mitigation: Introduce first_recorded_at on FindingRecord (step 2) and order exclusively against the exposure's wall-clock rendered_at. No iteration/cycle-number fallback exists anywhere in the matcher; absent timestamps yield indeterminate. Tests in step 11 cover multi-attempt pre-review, post-review dev retry, and review-cycle reset.

risks.description: Review context assembly may produce one shared context pack for multiple reviewer profiles.
risks.mitigation: Thread recipient role/profile metadata from review call sites and expand shared review context into per-recipient exposure records before persistence.

risks.description: Validation agreement could be circular if the labelled corpus is generated by the method it measures.
risks.mitigation: Hand-label the corpus from real persisted run artifacts before thresholds are written (step 5 precedes step 4), record per-example provenance and labeller, and include at least one known method miss so agreement is below 1.0.

risks.description: A lexical overlap method may under-match paraphrases or over-match common terms.
risks.mitigation: Keep the initial method deterministic, versioned, thresholded against the hand-labelled corpus, and report unvalidated status when the corpus cannot measure the active version.

risks.description: Backwards-compatible audit loading can accidentally make old runs look compared with zero matches.
risks.mitigation: Add an explicit pre-exposure-capture/uncomparable state in audit_storage.py migrations/readers and regression tests in tests/test_audit_storage_read_model_boundary.py asserting old records never enter the compared totals.
